note: Original write-ups for every High-confidence pick whose fair price falls inside the requested -250 to +10,000 window. Each cites only records, recent results and venue data from the official payloads listed in verification.json.

items.text: New York is 4-1-0 at UBS Arena and beat Anaheim 3-2 there on Tuesday, with only 20 goals allowed in nine starts. Los Angeles has 17 goals in seven games and was beaten 4-1 in Boston on Sunday. The Islanders moneyline is the side to take.

Pittsburgh has lost three straight road games by a combined 16-8 and sits on seven points from ten, with 38 goals conceded. Nashville won 5-2 in St. Louis last week and has only two regulation defeats. A Predators side that needs to avoid a two-goal loss is well priced.

Dallas has conceded just 15 goals in nine games and beat Boston 3-2 in overtime on Wednesday, so chances will be scarce in this one. New York is 5-3-1 and lost only three times all season. A 1.5-goal cushion on a team that keeps games tight looks generous.

Winnipeg has 24 goals in nine games, lost 3-2 at home to Carolina and then 2-1 in St. Louis. Florida carries 31 goals and a 3-2-2 road record, and its heaviest defeat came in Ottawa. The Panthers only need to stay within one goal at Canada Life Centre.

Chicago has shipped 36 goals in nine games, including a 4-0 home loss to Dallas, and owns only three wins. Los Angeles ended its slide with a 5-2 victory in Washington on Tuesday. Even at 1-4-2, the Kings should keep this inside one goal at United Center.

Dallas has allowed 15 goals in nine games and its latest outing was a 3-2 overtime win over Boston. New Jersey has 29 goals in nine, and its two recent defeats finished 4-3 and 4-2. Six and a half is a tall number for two teams whose games stay low, so the under 6.5 is the call.

Seattle has 39 goals in ten games and Toronto 38 in eleven, and the Kraken were beaten 8-3 in Florida last week. Toronto put six past Columbus and three past San Jose in its past two. Two attacking sides on a fast Seattle sheet makes over 5.5 the play.

These clubs met on Tuesday and combined for nine goals in Utah's 5-4 win, the third straight game in which Pittsburgh conceded five or more. Utah is scoring at nearly four a night with 38 in ten games, while Pittsburgh has shipped 38 in ten. Another open evening at PPG Paints Arena makes over 5.5 the play.

Minnesota has given up 25 goals in ten games and New York just 20 in nine, which are two of the tighter defensive records on the board. The Wild's latest game was a 4-3 overtime loss in Edmonton and the Islanders beat Anaheim 3-2. Seven goals is too many to ask, so take under 6.5.

Two of the meanest defensive records on this board meet here: Minnesota has conceded 25 times in ten outings, New York 20 in nine. The Wild's most recent game finished 4-3 after overtime in Edmonton, and the visitors won 3-2 against Anaheim. A 6.5 line asks too much of sides built on defence, so the under is the play.

Los Angeles is 0-3-0 at Crypto.com Arena and has managed 17 goals in seven games, roughly 2.4 a night. Buffalo has 28 goals in ten and took Montréal to overtime last week. The Sabres need only to avoid a two-goal defeat against the coldest home team in the league.

Calgary has conceded 37 goals in eight games, an average of 4.6, and lost 6-2 in Vegas before a 3-2 win in Carolina. Seattle has 39 goals in ten and scored four in Detroit on Tuesday. With the Flames defence leaking, the over 5.5 should not survive.

Columbus has 20 goals in eight games and is 0-2-0 on the road, most recently beaten 6-2 in Toronto. Dallas has allowed 15 goals in nine, beat Boston 3-2 in overtime and shut out Chicago 4-0. The Stars moneyline is the cleanest read on this slate.

Edmonton is 5-0-0 away from home with 41 goals in nine games and just won 4-3 in overtime in Minnesota. The Rangers are 6-0-0 at the Garden but lost 1-0 in overtime to Columbus there. The Oilers with a 1.5-goal start are the percentage call at MSG.

Edmonton has 41 goals in nine games, better than four and a half per night, and beat Utah 6-2 last week. New Jersey has 29 in nine and beat Colorado 4-3. Two attacking teams with leaky evenings in between point clearly to the over at five and a half.

Los Angeles has not won at home this season, going 0-3-0 with 17 goals in seven games, and lost 4-1 in Boston on Sunday. San Jose has 27 goals in ten and won 4-3 in overtime in Montréal. One goal of protection against the coldest home side is enough.

Anaheim has lost its last two, 3-2 on Long Island and 5-2 at the Rangers, and has 26 goals in nine games. Edmonton is 7-1-1 with 41 goals, has points in five straight and scored six against Utah. The Oilers moneyline at Rogers Place is straightforward.

Utah has 38 goals in ten games and won 5-4 in Pittsburgh on Tuesday, the second time this week it featured nine combined goals. Montréal has conceded 34 in nine and lost 4-3 in overtime to San Jose at the Bell Centre. Both defences are giving up chances.

Tampa Bay is 7-2-0 with 31 goals and 23 against, having won 6-2 in Vegas and 4-2 in Vancouver. Minnesota is unbeaten at home but has 31 goals in ten games and lost 4-3 in overtime in Edmonton last time out. The Lightning with a goal and a half start are the value.

Calgary has 17 goals in eight games while conceding 37, and its scores have rarely run high, including a 3-2 win in Carolina. Philadelphia has 20 goals in twelve and won 3-1 in Buffalo. Two of the least productive attacks in the league meeting in Calgary stays under 6.5.
